Lancet 1995; 345: 1275–7. Anthrax Anthrax is caused by Bacillus anthracis, a spore-forming Gram-positive aerobe found in the soil. It most commonly infects herbivorous mammals. Humans can become in- fected by contact with infected animals or infected or con- taminated animal products, or by inhalation of anthrax spores. Person-to-person transmission has not been report- ed. Although rare in western countries it remains a prob- lem in many areas, including Africa, Asia, some southern European countries, the Americas, and parts of Australia. Anthrax has also been used as a weapon for biological warfare. In humans anthrax presents most often in the cutaneous form.
